subject: Police Station Demolition And Fire Training Tower
overview: The council approved a controversial $1 million appropriation for the demolition of the police station and fire training tower to facilitate the construction of a new police headquarters. The meeting also addressed municipal building funding through a home rule petition and various neighborhood improvements.

items.title: Commendation and Business Licenses
items.summary: The council awarded a citation to Elizabeth Lazzaro for her hockey achievements and approved business and signage licenses for Target and Blink Fitness on Salem Street.

items.title: Hustle Killer Signage Resolution
items.summary: The council discussed the inappropriateness of a 'Hustle Killer' sign located near a school, noting it would be removed due to lack of a permit.

items.title: Municipal Appointments
items.summary: The council approved the appointment of Alex Gostanian as Commissioner of Trust Funds but tabled reappointments to the Community Preservation Commission until the candidates could appear in person.

items.title: Harris Park Improvement Appropriation
items.summary: Approved the first reading of an $817,000 project for Harris Park improvements, funded by a $300,000 state grant and existing Community Preservation Act funds.

items.title: Revolving Fund Ordinance Amendment
items.summary: Approved an amendment to the city ordinances establishing departmental revolving funds as required by the Municipal Modernization Act.

items.title: Home Rule Petition for Municipal Building Donations
items.summary: Approved a home rule petition to allow voluntary contribution check-off boxes on property tax bills for police, fire, and library building projects.

items.title: Lesley University Park Use Inquiry
items.summary: Approved a request for information and school committee records regarding the potential rental of Dugger Park and Tufts Park to Lesley University.

items.title: Police Station Demolition Appropriation
items.summary: Approved $1 million for the demolition of the police training tower and headquarters, a move heavily contested by fire union representatives who argued it removes essential training infrastructure without a replacement plan.

items.title: Roberts Elementary School Surfacing Project
items.summary: Tabled a request for $107,350 in Community Preservation Act funds for playground surfacing to the Committee of the Whole despite arguments regarding construction timing urgency.

items.title: Medford Square and Airport Noise Resolutions
items.summary: Approved the creation of an ad hoc committee for the Medford Square Master Plan and requested an update from the Massport Community Advisory Council regarding airplane noise impacts.

items.title: Fire Headquarters Debt Exclusion Language
items.summary: Tabled a resolution requesting draft language for a fire headquarters debt exclusion referendum following debate over the necessity of tax increases and the transparency of the proposal.

items.title: Red Flag Bill Support
items.summary: Approved a letter of support for House Bill 3610, which would allow family or law enforcement to petition the court to temporarily remove firearms from individuals deemed dangerous.

items.title: Inclusionary Zoning and Notification Report
items.summary: Adopted a committee report recommending affordable housing thresholds to the Zoning Board of Appeals and referring new developer notification signage rules to the Community Development board.
